title: Storage Security and Redundancy
description: Learn how to secure Azure Storage with keys, SAS tokens, RBAC, and choose the right replication strategy for your data durability needs.

data.text: Azure Storage is secure by default, but you need to understand the options available to control who can access your data and how your data is protected against hardware failures and disasters.

data.title: Ways to Secure Your Storage Account
items: **Storage account keys** — Two secret keys that give full access to the entire storage account. Treat them like passwords and rotate them regularly.
**Shared Access Signatures (SAS)** — Time-limited, permission-scoped tokens that let you grant access to specific resources without sharing your keys.
**Azure RBAC (Role-Based Access Control)** — Grants permissions to Azure AD identities at the storage account, container, or blob level.

cards.title: Account Keys
cards.description: Two master keys that provide full access to all storage services.

cards.title: SAS Token
cards.description: A scoped, time-limited URL that grants specific permissions to specific resources.

cards.title: RBAC
cards.description: Azure AD-based role assignments at the account, container, or blob level.

data.text: Azure replicates your data to protect against hardware failures, data center outages, and regional disasters. The replication type you choose determines how many copies exist and where they are located.

rows: Zone-level resilience without extra read cost
Full disaster recovery with read access

terms.definition: A token that grants limited access to Azure Storage resources without exposing account keys
Role-Based Access Control — managing who can do what using Azure AD identities
Locally Redundant Storage — three copies within a single data center
Geo-Redundant Storage — six copies across two paired regions

data.title: Generate a SAS Token and Set RBAC with Azure CLI
data.content: These commands demonstrate generating a read-only SAS token and assigning a storage Blob Data Reader role.
data.code:
# Generate a SAS token for a container (read-only, valid for 1 hour)
az storage container generate-sas \
  --account-name mystorageaccount123 \
  --name mycontainer \
  --permissions r \
  --expiry 2025-12-31T23:59Z \
  --https-only

# Create a user-assigned identity for your app (if needed)
az identity create --name myAppIdentity --resource-group myResourceGroup

# Assign the 'Storage Blob Data Reader' role to the identity
az role assignment create \
  --assignee <principal-id> \
  --role 'Storage Blob Data Reader' \
  --scope /subscriptions/<sub-id>/resourceGroups/myResourceGroup/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/mystorageaccount123/blobServices/default/containers/mycontainer

# Rotate account keys
az storage account keys rotate \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --account-name mystorageaccount123 \
  --key secondary

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use SAS tokens for time-limited, scoped access instead of sharing account keys
RBAC with Azure AD is the most secure option for enterprise apps
LRS is cost-effective for most workloads within a single region
GRS or RA-GRS adds cross-region disaster recovery
data.takeaway: Start with RBAC and LRS for development, then add SAS tokens and upgrade replication as your production needs grow.
